title: Responses and errors
content_data:
## API response Events API 2.0 returns a response with the following fields: ``` xtable |Field{20%}|Data Type{20%}|Description{60%}| |---|---|---| |code |number|Response code. For the complete list of response codes and descriptions, see [Appendix-Return Code](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737172488964097). | |message|string|Response message. For details, see [Appendix - Return Codes](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737172488964097).| |request_id |string|The log ID of a request, which uniquely identifies the request. | |data |object|Returned data.
For a successful request, this field will be an empty object (`{}`).
For a failed request, this field will not be returned.| ``` ## API response codes For a full list of possible API response codes returned by TikTok API for Business, refer to [Appendix - Return Codes](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737172488964097). ### For successful calls If the event is received successfully by TikTok, the API will return a response with `200` HTTP Status Code. The response body will contain an API response code (TikTok API for Business return code) of `0`. ```xtable | Return code{20%} | HTTP Status Code{20%} | Description{30%} | Detail {30%}| |---|---|---|---| | 0 | 200 | Successful | Request succeeded. | ``` #### Example ```xcodeblock (code curl http) HTTP 1.1 200 OK { "code": 0, "message": "OK", "request_id": "{{request_id}}", "data":{} } (/code) ``` ### For failed calls If the request fails, you will get a `4XX` or `5XX` HTTP Status Code. The response body will contain a corresponding return code and a message explaining the details about the failure. Check the `message` field in the response body for error details. If multiple events are sent in the same API call, the `message` field will also indicate the index (zero-based) of the first invalid event. For example, the error message below suggests that the **third** event's `event_id` is not a valid string. ```xcodeblock (code) { "code":40002, "message":"Invalid value for data.2.event_id: not a valid string.", "request_id":"202308291437415F6E70BA7E095091A6F4" } (/code) ``` Below is a list of commonly seen errors for Events API 2.0: ```xtable | Return Code{20%} | HTTP Status Code {20%}| Error reason{60%} | |---|---|---| | 40001 | 400 | No permission.
You don't not have the necessary permission to operate the advertiser account. | | 40002 | 400 | Invalid payload.

Common causes:
  • The payload is not a valid JSON.
  • Missing required field or wrong field type (for instance, passing in string when a number is required).
  • An unhashed value is used for a field (for instance, `email`) that requires SHA256 hashing
  • Sending too many events (>1000) in a single request.
| | 40100 | 401 | Too many requests (exceeded API quota limit).

Common causes:
  • The rate limit for the endpoint (1,000 queries per second) has been reached, thus your request is throttled.
| | 40104 | 401 | Access token is empty. | ``` #### Example ```xcodeblock (code curl http) HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request { "code": 40002 "message": "Invalid value for email: not a valid SHA256-hashed string." "request_id": "{{request_id}}" } (/code) ``` `
